task.description: Independently verify REQ-226's tenant-scoped migration and CRUD module against all applicable security invariants, and characterize the flagged content-hash dedup discrepancy.

result.note:
Scope test: applies (new tenant-scoped table entity_definitions + migration + CRUD context). Assessed INV-1..INV-9 against git diff main...HEAD (bcd80e23):

INV-1 (tenant isolation) -- APPLIES, PASS. (a) prefix-scoping confirmed: definitions.ex create_definition/2 -> Repo.insert(...,prefix: prefix) L164; get_definition/2 -> Repo.get(EntityDefinition, id, prefix: prefix) L185; get_definition_by_name/2 -> Repo.one(query, prefix: prefix) L205; list_definitions/2 -> Repo.all(..., prefix: prefix) L242 plus explicit where([e], e.tenant_id == ^tenant_id) L238; activate_definition/4 -> Repo.update(prefix: prefix) L337. get_definition/2 and get_definition_by_name/2 rely on prefix-scoping alone (no redundant tenant_id WHERE) -- traced this is the established codebase-wide idiom for single-record Repo.get/Repo.one lookups (lib/letflow/dlq.ex:203, lib/letflow/instances.ex:63, lib/letflow/webhooks.ex:692, lib/letflow/identity.ex multiple, lib/letflow/definitions.ex multiple all do the same), not a REQ-226-specific gap. No cross-tenant read/write path found. (b) migration guarded by `if prefix() do` (create_entity_definitions.exs L34) and registered in Letflow.TenantProvisioning's @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest (tenant_provisioning.ex L492-494, confirmed via git diff) -- not reachable in public schema. (c) tenant_id is derived from the resolved prefix at write time via TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(prefix) (definitions.ex L113, L184, L202, L233) in every function, never accepted as a separate caller-supplied field -- create_definition/2's attrs map (create_attrs type) has no tenant_id key at all.

INV-2 -- NOT-APPLICABLE (no route/controller layer added; S4 API surface not started).
INV-3 -- NOT-APPLICABLE (S5 not started).
INV-4 (secrets) -- APPLIES (live invariant), PASS. grep for System.get_env/password/secret/token across the 3 new/changed lib files: zero hits. No secret material touched by this change.
INV-5 -- NOT-APPLICABLE (no lookup-by-ID API endpoint; this is an internal context module, S4 not started).
INV-6 (new data-access path proves scoping) -- APPLIES, PASS (this handoff itself is the proof).
INV-7 (no raw SQL) -- APPLIES, PASS. grep -rn 'Repo.query' across lib/ and priv/repo/migrations/ for this diff's files: zero hits. Migration uses only Ecto.Migration DSL (create table/index, references) with prefix: schema, a trusted Ecto-resolved value, not string-interpolated. Definitions.ex uses only Ecto.Query composition (where/order_by/limit macros), all parameterised (^name, ^tenant_id, ^page_size etc.).
INV-8 (no unhandled crashes) -- APPLIES, PASS. grep for the '{:ok, ...} = ' heuristic found no hits in lib/letflow/entities/definitions.ex or entity_definition.ex. One instance in the REQ-225 Shape module (shape.ex:78, out of this diff's scope but read for the dedup question below): `{:ok, canonical_form} = Canonicaliser.canonicalize_content("application/json", json_bytes)` where json_bytes = Jason.encode!(document) -- Jason.encode! always produces syntactically valid JSON, and canonicalize_content's json branch only fails on Jason.decode error, so this pattern-match cannot raise on any input reachable through this path (equivalent to 'immediately after a value the same function already validated', per INV-8's own carve-out). Not a defect.
INV-9 -- NOT-APPLICABLE (no outbound HTTP request).

Content/data integrity check (task item 7): UNIQUE (tenant_id, name, logical_shape_version) constraint confirmed present at the DB level via create unique_index(:entity_definitions, [:tenant_id, :name, :logical_shape_version], name: :entity_definitions_tenant_name_shape_idx, prefix: schema) in the migration (L65-70), and enforced at the application layer via EntityDefinition.changeset/2's unique_constraint(:name, name: @unique_tenant_name_shape_constraint_name) (entity_definition.ex L77) which translates the DB constraint violation into {:error, {:persistence, changeset}} rather than silently swallowing it. A concurrent-create race for the same (tenant_id, name, logical_shape_version) is safely handled: both inserts reach Repo.insert, the DB constraint rejects the loser, and the loser's changeset error surfaces as {:error, {:persistence, changeset}} -- no silent duplicate possible. ELIXIR-DEV's own handoff states this was exercised via mix test (71 tests passing across definitions_test.exs/repository_test.exs/activation_test.exs).

Scenario A / content_hash dedup discrepancy: verified independently by reading lib/letflow/entities/definition/shape.ex in full. content_hash/1 (L44-46) calls hash_via_canonicaliser(definition) directly on the *entire* definition document (via Jason.encode!(document) at L77) with no field-stripping -- unlike logical_shape_of/1 (L61-65) which explicitly Map.drops @non_logical_fields ([:display_name, :description]) before hashing but does NOT drop :name either. So content_hash includes :name, confirming ELIXIR-DEV's flag: two EntityDefinition documents differing only in `name` produce different content_hash values, and create_definition/2 (definitions.ex L119) passes that same `name` as Repository.create/2's artifact_name, which Repository.create/2 uses as-is (repository.ex L124-144, upsert_content keyed on the computed hash L130). Therefore the design doc's Scenario A ('two definitions, different names, one shared repository_artifacts row') is structurally unreachable through this pipeline; only Scenario B (identical name+shape resubmission, rejected by the UNIQUE constraint after a redundant artifact_versions row) is reachable, and is what the shipped tests (definitions_test.exs) actually exercise.

Characterization: this is NOT a security finding. No cross-tenant exposure, no secret leakage, no SQL injection, no authorization bypass, and no unbounded/attacker-controlled resource exhaustion results from it -- the repository_artifacts dedup that fails to trigger here is a storage-efficiency optimisation (avoiding a second content row for byte-identical content under two different artifact names), not an isolation or integrity boundary; the actual integrity boundary (no two rows for the same tenant/name/shape) is still enforced by the DB UNIQUE constraint regardless of this gap. A tenant that legitimately creates N distinct entity-definition names already consumes N artifact_versions rows whether or not cross-name dedup works, so this does not enable unbounded storage growth beyond what unique legitimate names already require. This is a design-vs-implementation documentation mismatch in an already-validated design artifact (AC4's 'different name, shared hash' clause is unimplementable given REQ-225's Shape module as shipped) and is correctly routed to REVIEWER for sign-off per ELIXIR-DEV's own handoff, not something SECURITY-REVIEWER blocks on.

Overall: no BLOCKER found on any applicable invariant. status: PASS.
